items.headline: SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5, a Cursor-trained frontier coding model
items.diff_narrative: Today's coding-stack story inverts yesterday's. On July 8 the coding-agent news was Simon Willison's llm-coding-agent, a dependency-light harness collapsing the category's floor toward a self-hostable, single-maintainer loop decoupled from any one vendor. Today SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5, a frontier model co-trained with Cursor on trillions of tokens of the IDE-agent's own usage data and shipped as Cursor's same-day default across desktop, web, iOS, CLI, and SDK, priced at $2/$6 per million tokens to undercut incumbents and ranking fourth of 168 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at 54. Where yesterday pushed the harness open and downward, today fuses the model and harness layers upward into one vertically integrated product; the only continuity is the shared coding-agent beat.

items.headline: SK Hynix and CXMT launch back-to-back memory-chip IPOs
items.diff_narrative: A net-new capital-markets thread with no antecedent in yesterday's edition, which carried no memory, HBM, or IPO coverage. Two mega-listings land in the same week: SK Hynix's roughly $28B US ADR offering (expected to price July 10 and trade July 11, book more than seven times oversubscribed, revenue up nearly 200% year-over-year) and China DRAM leader CXMT's roughly $4.3B Shanghai listing (book-building from July 15, revenue up 700% year-over-year). The throughline is that AI-infrastructure capital is moving one layer beneath the accelerator into the DRAM and HBM that feed it, whereas yesterday's infrastructure coverage sat at the software layer with vLLM serving and Unsloth tuning.

items.headline: JADEPUFFER: first ransomware run end-to-end by an autonomous AI agent
items.diff_narrative: The security beat shifts from a static vulnerability disclosure to a live agentic intrusion. Yesterday's security item was CVE-2026-10539, an unpatched CVSS 9.5 command-injection flaw in BMC Control-M/Server framed as a positional risk with no observed exploitation. Today Sysdig documents JADEPUFFER, which it characterizes as the first ransomware campaign executed end-to-end by an LLM-driven agent rather than a human operator: it chained the known Langflow RCE (CVE-2025-3248) into API-key and credential theft, lateral movement, a secondary Nacos exploit, and destructive encryption, with roughly 600 purpose-built payloads carrying LLM-style code comments as the tell. The framing moves from 'here is a dangerous bug' to 'an agent already weaponized one,' recasting agentic AI as offensive tooling.

items.headline: CISA KEV patch sprint led by a max-severity ColdFusion RCE
items.diff_narrative: A second, distinct security story with no prior-day antecedent. Where yesterday tracked a single CVE at the advisory stage, today CISA adds four actively exploited flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on July 8 with a July 10 federal patch deadline, an unusually short window. It is headlined by CVE-2026-48282, a CVSS 10.0 Adobe ColdFusion path-traversal RCE reportedly exploited within hours of disclosure, alongside two more 10.0 Joomla file-upload RCEs and a Langflow authorization-bypass (CVE-2026-55255). That Langflow entry ties directly to today's JADEPUFFER item, doubling the day's agent-framework exposure; the shift versus yesterday is from disclosed-but-quiet to exploited-in-hours.

items.headline: Zeroth raises $74M (Ant Group) for home and education humanoids
items.diff_narrative: A net-new robotics thread absent from yesterday's edition. Chinese humanoid-robotics startup Zeroth raised about $74M in pre-Series A funding led by Ant Group, with Geely Capital and others participating, reporting more than 30,000 robot orders and roughly 600% year-over-year H1 revenue growth on M1 and W1 units sold into early-childhood education, smart-home, and pet-companionship uses. The data point argues the humanoid market is bifurcating by geography and use case, China's consumer and education demand center versus the West's factory-floor pitch, a topic the prior day did not touch.

items.headline: AI events: ICML Seoul workshops close the weekend; fall tracks stack up
items.diff_narrative: The recurring events roundup carries over from yesterday with a refreshed status and new venues. ICML has moved from 'main conference wrapping today' on July 8 to its main program wrapped at COEX with only the July 10-11 workshops still live for the weekend, and NeurIPS in Sydney this December is now flagged as the next marquee research venue. The AI Conference (Pier 48, Sep 29 to Oct 1) and Anyscale's late-August Ray Summit are newly named; the Hot Chips July 31 early-registration deadline is nearer, while the August security cluster (AI Risk Summit Aug 11-12, Black Hat and DEF CON) and the enterprise track (Ai4 Aug 4-6, GitHub Universe, AWS re:Invent) carry forward from yesterday.
